`./compile.sh` reports **`compiled OK`**.

## What was produced

`tests/org/apache/commons/lang/StringEscapeUtilsAgentTest.java` — a single self-contained JUnit 4 test class (matching `junit-4.12` in `lib/`), in the same package, with **83 `@Test` methods** covering every method in the javadoc spec.

### Coverage, all anchored to the `api/` contract

| Area | What is asserted |
|---|---|
| `escapeJava` / `escapeJavaScript` (String) | null→null, `""`→`""`, plain text unchanged, tab→`\t`, cr→`\r`, nl→`\n`, ff→`\f`, `\`→`\\`, `"`→`\"`; single quote **not** escaped by `escapeJava` but **is** by `escapeJavaScript`; both javadoc examples verbatim; and the documented "only difference is the single quote" invariant checked directly. |
| Writer overloads | output equals the String overload; null string → nothing written (for the four methods that document "no effect"); **null Writer → `IllegalArgumentException`** for all 8 Writer methods; `IOException` from a broken `Writer` propagates (inner `BrokenWriter` fixture). |
| `unescapeJava` / `unescapeJavaScript` | `\n`→newline, `\t`→tab, `\\`→`\`, `\\n` stays `\n` (the "preceded by another `\`" rule), `\u0041`→`A`, `\"`→`"`, `\'`→`'`; round-trips with the matching escape. |
| `escapeHtml` / `unescapeHtml` | javadoc example, `&`/`<`/`>` entities, apostrophe **not** escaped (`'` unsupported), accented letter → `é`, `©` → `©`, `A`→`A`, unrecognized `&zzzz;` left verbatim, round-trip. |
| `escapeXml` / `unescapeXml` | javadoc example, exactly the five basic entities incl. `'` (contrasted with HTML), plain ASCII unchanged, no named HTML entities emitted, round-trip. Non-ASCII `\u` behaviour is deliberately **not** pinned (javadoc marks it unstable). |
| `escapeSql` | null→null, javadoc example `McHale's Navy`→`McHale''s Navy`, every `'` doubled, `%`/`_`/`"`/`\` left untouched. |
| constructor | public and usable (as the javadoc states). |

Non-ASCII characters the spec mentions ("funky accents") are built from code points via a private `ch(int)` helper so the source stays pure ASCII and compiles under any file encoding.
